newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- With Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan ready to detail deep budget cuts for the current fiscal year to the Cabinet this morning, a senior military officer and the interior minister say that they are prepared to accept cuts to their agencies' budgets. Apart from the budget issue, the Cabinet is also due to make decisions on two other highly-sensitive matters - the Nong Ngu Hao second airport project and the administrative court.

- The Public Health Ministry has alerted provincial health authorities to closely monitor the spread of anthrax, particularly in border provinces, following a report of six new cases in Sukhothai province. The public is also warned to avoid low-priced beef since it could come from cattle smuggled into the country. Meanwhile, health authorities in Tak are preparing to vaccinate tens of thousands of cattle to contain the spread of anthrax after cows sent from the northern province to Bangkok were found to be contaminated. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- A police warrant for the arrest of former interior minister Suchart Tancharoen - in connection with the land scandal in northeastern province of Nong Khai for alleged abuse of authority - has been approved. Investigators will ask the Interior Ministry to coordinate with Parliament for Suchart's arrest. (BANGKOK POST)

- Plans to cut 99 billion baht off this year's fiscal budget will have a minimal impact on Thailand's economic growth, says secretary-general of the National Economic and Social Development Board. He says the cutbacks to be considered by the cabinet today will trim growth by no more than 0.1 percentage points this year. The board has previously predicted 7.1 percent growth in gross domestic product. (BANGKOK POST)

- Construction of the Petro Chain (Thailand) naptha splitter project is being delayed by negotiations among the partners on the shareholding structure. A conclusion is expected to be reached within two months on the proportion of shares to be held by Petro Chain (Thailand), which was formed in April last year, by Siam Chemicals and Siam Cement Chemical, an Siam Cement subsidiary. The other co-founders are the Crown Property Bureau and Siam Commercial Bank. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The government may consider renegotiating its controversial 11 billion baht Nong Ngu Hao international airport land-preparation contract with Italian-Thai Development Plc, if Cabinet today approves an expansion plan for Don Muang airport and amendments to the second airport project. On the land preparation contract, it is understood that an expansion of Don Muang will justify a further delay of the Nong Ngu Hao project and, possibly, a project scale-down to lower land preparation costs because less sand will be needed. (THE NATION)
